sections.h2: Who handles property tax questions in Vermilion County?
sections.html:
Vermilion County divides property tax questions among four offices in Danville, and the Treasurer's page names each one. Calling the right one first saves a transfer.

  • County Clerk, 217-554-1903: tax rates, tax codes and delinquent property tax information.
  • Recorder, 217-554-6040: deed information.
  • Supervisor of Assessments, 217-554-1940: name and address changes, assessed values and exemptions.
  • Treasurer, 217-554-6080: tax bill and payment information.

The Treasurer keeps hours Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding legal holidays. The Supervisor of Assessments sits on the third floor of the Joseph G. Cannon Building at 201 North Vermilion Street, where the Board of Review also takes filings.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Vermilion County?
sections.html:
Vermilion County runs along the Indiana line between the state border and Champaign County. It was incorporated on January 18, 1826, as the 45th of Illinois' 102 counties, and at 901 square miles it ranks as the seventh largest. Danville is the seat and largest city. The county's name comes from the Vermilion River, and Lake Vermilion, a 1,000-acre reservoir northwest of Danville, supplies the city's water.

The 2020 census counted 74,188 people, and the 2025 estimate is 71,259. The county has 34,407 housing units, 11.2 percent of them vacant, and 67.8 percent of occupied homes are owned. Danville Area Community College is in the county.

Interstate 74 passes along Danville's southern edge, with U.S. 136, U.S. 150 and Illinois Route 1 meeting downtown. Four rail lines cross the Danville area, so crossings near a house can matter to a buyer. Abraham Lincoln practiced law in Danville from 1841 to 1859, and the Fithian home, where he once spoke, is now the Vermilion County Museum. Twelve school districts serve the county.

sections.h2: What were the Vermilion County 2026 tax payment dates?
sections.html:
The first installment was due Thursday, June 18, 2026. The second, and mobile home taxes, were due Friday, September 4. The Treasurer then set a series of cutoffs ahead of the sale.

Checks are made payable to Vermilion County Treasurer, and the phone payment line is 1 (877) 221-8591. Owners who want electronic bills can register at vermilion.mcgedoc.com using the code printed on their current statement.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Vermilion County assessment?
sections.html:
A complaint on a 2026 assessment has to reach the Board of Review within 30 calendar days after the township assessor and Supervisor of Assessments publish their changes. The board follows the statute, 35 ILCS 200/16-55, and its rules for the 2026 assessment year fill in the practical steps.

  • File on the board's approved form, in duplicate, with a complete copy of every document you want considered.
  • Use a separate form for each tract number. The form covers residential, commercial and industrial property, and farmland has its own form.
  • File in person, email brdreview@vercounty.org, or mail it to 201 North Vermilion St, 3rd Floor, Danville, IL 61832.
  • The complainant must have owned the property on January 1 of the assessment year.

A complaint filed in 2026 affects the 2026 assessment, which is the basis for the bill payable in 2027. The 2026 bill rests on the 2025 assessment. The board cannot change a tax rate and will not hear complaints about one.

sections.h2: What happens after a Vermilion County complaint is filed?
sections.html:
The board reviews the complaint and the attached papers, may look at the property, and mails a Notice of Proposed Decision. An owner who is not satisfied must ask for a hearing in writing within 10 days of the date on that notice, using the board's form.

A Notice of Hearing then goes out at least 10 days before the hearing date. Missing the hearing means dismissal. Anyone seeking a reduction of $100,000 or more in assessed value on a parcel, or a combination of parcels, is advised to use an attorney.

The board's rules also address appraisals. Any appraisal must meet the Real Estate Appraiser Licensing Act and USPAP, state whether the appraiser is licensed in Illinois, and list the board and Vermilion County as intended users when it supports a complaint. The board will not issue a certificate of error for a mere error of judgment in valuation. After the board decides, a further appeal can go to the state Property Tax Appeal Board within 30 days of written notice of the decision (35 ILCS 200/16-160).

sections.h2: How does the Supervisor of Assessments organize Vermilion County values?
sections.html:
The Supervisor of Assessments office was created by state law to give statistical and performance data to the Illinois Department of Revenue and technical advice to the township assessors and the Board of Review. It keeps the name and address records, assessed values and exemptions, equalizes assessments, and acts as clerk of the Board of Review. It publishes the assessment change notices and mails them to taxpayers.

Vermilion County posts a 2023 quadrennial assessment roll, payable in 2024, for 19 townships: Blount, Butler, Carroll, Catlin, Danville, Elwood, Georgetown, Grant, Jamaica, Love, McKendree, Middlefork, Newell, Oakwood, Pilot, Ross, Sidell, South Ross and Vance. A parcel's township determines which assessor owns the first look at its value.

sections.h2: What tax relief does Vermilion County point owners to?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's relief page lists two programs. The first is the Senior Citizens and Disabled Persons Property Tax Relief and Pharmaceutical Assistance Act, with applications from the Illinois Department of Revenue at 800-624-2459. The second is the Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program, and its applications are available in the Treasurer's office at 217-554-6080.

Exemptions that lower the assessed value, such as the homestead exemptions, go through the Supervisor of Assessments instead. The county also posts an application for a general homestead exemption on single-family dwellings subject to a lease.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Vermilion County taxes?
sections.html:
The first installment goes delinquent after its due date and bears interest at 1 1/2 percent per month or portion of a month, as 35 ILCS 200/21-15 sets for counties of this size. Later in the fall the county publishes names of unpaid owners and holds a sale of the taxes, in 2026 on November 4.

The buyer at that sale holds a tax lien, and the owner can redeem. For certificates issued on or after January 1, 2024, 35 ILCS 200/21-350 sets the period at 3 years from the date of sale, with exceptions. The County Clerk at 217-554-1903 handles delinquent property tax information, so ask there before a closing.

A Vermilion County house with taxes due can sell as is for cash. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When were Vermilion County property taxes due in 2026?
faqs.a: The first installment was due June 18, 2026, and the second installment and mobile home taxes were due September 4. The Treasurer stopped taking payments after November 3.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a Vermilion County assessment complaint?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days after publication of the assessment changes for your township. The complaint goes to the Board of Review in duplicate on its form, with supporting documents attached.

faqs.q: Can the Vermilion County Board of Review lower my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The board has no authority to change a tax rate and does not consider complaints about rates. It reviews only the assessed value of the property.

faqs.q: Who do I call about delinquent taxes in Vermilion County?
faqs.a: Call the County Clerk at 217-554-1903 for delinquent property tax information. For payment and bill questions, the Treasurer's number is 217-554-6080.

faqs.q: Is there a deferral program for seniors in Vermilion County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer lists a Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program, and applications are available at that office. The Illinois Department of Revenue also supplies applications for the Senior Citizens and Disabled Persons relief act.
